chapter: Lee Collins and the riverboat Washington
title: Excursions to Harrisonburg and rough crowds
summary: He describes rough crowds, a threat to Ben Allen and the piano player.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Yeah, they danced on the boat. Well we used to give excursions, our first excursions from New Orleans would be at Harrisonburg. Well Harrisonburg, the jungle is 22 miles, and at Harrisonburg, oh there used to be some rough people used to come on there. There'd be some people come over there, but you couldn't go over on that side because handling all that brulee whiskey, you know, and the little Lionel, there's a nobody come over there. Well I had made it good with them people who had old Ben Allen, this boy playing piano. They wanted to throw him overboard over there, but I begged them not to throw him overboard. They made the captain get up out the bed and everything out there. And I used to be all right with them people. When the crowd would get around me too much, the crowds would get around and cheer, I said, watch out, they ain't got smallpox, you understand? Make them kids get back. Well if they got too many around you might turn the boat over.

No, no, me talking about children, they used to be bringing in children. We used to have some, but I see one night that old man Humphrey Willis' daddy was on the boat. He made a trip in Martin Cole's place, and we went out there and got drunk. He said, you know, the bitch looked like he was going to put, you know, the bonkers, he said, watch out, don't you drive?
